title: Does independent-root counting predict token survival better than voice counting?
frozenBefore: any token was collected under this rule
whyFrozenFirst: Collecting is not analysing, but a rule written after looking at the data is a rule chosen knowing what it does. Freezing it first means the collector runs mechanically and cannot be steered. The pilot (RUN-20260811-1) violated this: its 14-day death threshold was chosen while looking at the data, which is why that run is exploratory and not a result.

population.frame: every SPL token whose initializeMint/initializeMint2 appears in a contiguous block range, top-level or inner instruction
population.blockRange: declared at collection start and recorded in the manifest; not extended after any outcome is inspected

livenessFilter.rule: a token enters the analysed population only if it has at least MIN_DISTINCT_SIGNERS distinct signing accounts transacting against its mint within LIVENESS_WINDOW_HOURS of creation
livenessFilter.why: The pilot measured an 88% death rate because the frame included tokens that never launched at all. They die for reasons unrelated to backing independence and leave a predictor no room to be wrong. This filter is the outcome-side counterpart to BL-060: a population whose outcome barely varies cannot test a predictor, however sound.

rootMeasure.voiceCount: distinct signing accounts that transacted against the mint
rootMeasure.rootCount: voices collapsed by funding cluster: two accounts are the same root if they share a funding ancestor within MAX_HOPS, after excluding hub funders

hubExclusion.rule: a funder is a HUB and is never used to merge roots if its full history exceeds HUB_MIN_TX or it has funded more than HUB_MIN_FANOUT distinct accounts
hubExclusion.why: Fifty accounts funded from one exchange are fifty people. Collapsing them would make the method appear predictive for a reason that has nothing to do with independence. The pilot could not measure this: 14 of 32 funders exceeded a 4,000-transaction cap, so their true size was unknown. An archival endpoint is required, and a funder whose history cannot be fully retrieved is treated as a HUB -- failing closed, since merging on unknown evidence is the error that matters.

outcome.definition: hours from creation until the mint is unresolvable, its supply is zero, or no transaction touches it for DEATH_IDLE_HOURS; right-censored at OBSERVATION_HOURS
outcome.why: A binary alive/dead at one instant discards each token's trajectory and has little power at an extreme base rate. Time to death uses the whole path. DEATH_IDLE_HOURS is set to 336 -- fourteen days -- which is the pilot's threshold, adopted deliberately rather than re-tuned, because changing it now would be choosing a threshold with knowledge of what the old one produced.
outcome.secondary: peakMultiple, if pool reserves prove derivable; NOT required for the primary endpoint and not a fallback if the primary fails

endpoint.H0: root count predicts time to death no better than voice count
endpoint.test: compare predictive performance of rootCount against voiceCount on the same conditioned population, same outcome
endpoint.passCondition: root count is a better predictor by the registered margin
endpoint.failCondition: it is not -- and this is a real possible answer the design must be able to produce

effectRequires.property: voice count and root count disagree
effectRequires.measuredInPilot: 1.45x inflation, 17 of 47 deployers launched more than one token, 56% of tokens -- SATISFIED before this run

effectRequires.rule: death rate in the conditioned population must fall between 20% and 80%
effectRequires.why: the pilot's 88% is outside this band. If the liveness filter does not bring it inside, the run STOPS and reports that, rather than proceeding with an outcome that cannot be predicted.

stopRule: collection ends at the declared block range or when the outcome-variance requirement is shown unsatisfiable, whichever is first. The range is not extended to obtain a result.
priorRun: RUN-20260811-1 pilot: n=68, 88% death, repeat-deployer 87% vs single 90%, p=1.000. Exploratory only -- its death threshold was chosen while looking at the data. It establishes feasibility and base rates, not a result.
